newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium stock falls may be re-distribution.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium stock falls may be re-distribution.

text.p: Consistent falls in aluminium inventories, both on terminal markets and at producers, do not tell the whole story, which may be why the price is under-performing, broker Macquarie Equities Ltd said.
Since the start of the year total reported primary stocks have fallen by some 493,000 tonnes, surpassing the most bullish of predictions.
"However, the performance of aluminium prices has not matched the stock draw-downs," Macquarie said in its latest weekly report.

The broker said there could be several reasons for this, including concerns over possible re-starts of the 800,000 tonnes of idled capacity, forward producer selling, worries over weaker demand, and the possible build of large "hidden" stocks by banks and traders into non-LME warehouses.

"Estimates of the amount of aluminium being held in these unreported stocks varies widely and there is often a confusion over the level of unreported stocks (perhaps one million tonnes plus and changes in the stocks over a defined period of time - 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes since September 1996?)," the broker said.

The stock transfers could reflect cheaper warehousing rates to maximise returns or an attempt to tighten availability and drive up premiums in order to maximise returns on their investments, Macquarie said.
